name_note: The GTDB genus Serratia carries the same name in the literature; the work cited here concerns its species Serratia marcescens.

sentences.text: Serratia marcescens is a Gram-negative opportunistic pathogen that causes healthcare-associated infections in neonatal intensive care units.

A review reports that intensive-care-associated infections with this organism frequently involve respiratory tract colonization, ventilator-associated pneumonia, bloodstream infection, urinary tract infection and device-related transmission.
The same review describes hospital water systems, sink drains, wet surfaces and ventilator circuits as persistent reservoirs, with biofilm formation supporting long-term survival.
A systematic review of neonates reported prematurity and very low birth weight as risk factors for infection or colonization, while breastfeeding and vaginal delivery were protective.
In one neonatal unit, whole-genome sequencing after an outbreak found only one infection over the following two years genetically linked to the original outbreak strain.
